text.p: This is how major world bond markets were trading in late European business on Thursday.

GERMANY - Bunds remained weak in late trade after slipping at the open on an overnight decline in U.S. Treasuries but dealers said the German market was well supported and some predicted slight gains on Friday. The June Bund future on the London International Financial Futures and Options Exchange (LIFFE) was trading at 101.44, down 0.34 from Wednesday's settlement price.

BRITAIN - Gilt futures ended weaker after another lacklustre range-bound session in which they took their cue mainly from the United States. The June long gilt future on LIFFE was trading at 111-04/32, down 11/32 from Wednesday's settlement price.

FRANCE - Ten-year bond futures settled lower as U.S. Treasuries beat a retreat on strong retail sales and jobs data that appeared to lend credence to arguments for a rise in American interest rates. The March notional bond future on the MATIF in Paris settled at 130.78, down 0.28 from Wednesday's settlement price.

ITALY - Italian Btp bond futures ended firmer, though off session highs, with the market reassured that domestic political tension appeared to recede for the moment. The June bond future on LIFFE was trading at 126.05, up 0.27 from Wednesday's settlement price.

UNITED STATES - U.S. Treasuries opened a bit weaker, with this morning's data expected to move the market out of the tight ranges seen for more than a week. The June Treasury bond future on the Chicago Board of Trade was trading at 108-30/32, down 23/32 from Wednesday's settlement price. The long bond was quoted to yield 6.94 percent.

JAPAN - The key June 10-year Japanese government bond futures contract ended just off its day's high, due to hectic cash bond buying from banks and brokers. In after hours trading the June future on LIFFE was trading at 126.32, up 0.51 from Wednesday's settlement price on the Tokyo Stock Exchange.

EUROBONDS - The formal launch of Russia's debut mark Eurobond, only its second international offering, was the primary market highlight. The deal's nine percent coupon was seen as a key element. Brazil will issue a 500 billion lire 10-year bond in May. Portugal set its expected French franc offering, an issue that will be redenominated in euros after EMU. Other activity included a raft of structured mark deals. The Asian markets saw the second issue denominated in Philippine pesos in a week.
